timingBoundary: The unchanged benchmark compiles each workload before its VM loop. Each VM constructor also finishes before performance.now(); the measured region is vm.run().

metadataInspection.comparisonLevel: Raw source instruction vectors and decoded CIL opcode/operand sequences; method names, owners and local/handler counts. This does not claim whole-PE or complete metadata/signature identity.

staticFindings: The source and direct-CIL dispatcher files, direct call/intrinsic handlers and ordinary AssemblyInspector are unchanged from the baseline.
The standalone benchmark instantiates neither loadProjectAssembly/createProjectAssemblyInspector nor Studio worker/debugger navigation helpers.

All four source method streams and CIL instruction operands and local/handler counts are identical between the inspected trees; no new property tables, external references or qualified source types are present.

Canonical member-profile metadata adds 172 bytes to each #SF stream. PE alignment adds 512 bytes to dictionary/list/builder; the 4096-byte builder PE becomes 4608 bytes (+12.5%). Emission and constructor parsing/verification are outside the timed interval.

MethodTableRegistry adds two identity fields during table materialization and passes its nullable registered-name index to normalization. The trie is allocated only for assembly-qualified definitions. Existing tables, descriptor indexes and instruction dispatch caches remain; no per-instruction graph map or closure is introduced.
conclusion: No newly executed graph/property/debug-provenance preparation was found in the timed standalone workloads. Source dictionary/list per-pair directions are inconsistent; CIL StringBuilder is slower in both pairs. These facts do not establish that infrastructure explains the regression. Causality among normalization/object-layout effects and shared-process resource pressure remains unresolved; no speculative runtime change was made.
remainingReview: Three pooled-median rows exceed the 5% contribution budget. Preserve the raw/per-pair results for a quiet-machine causal profile and explicit PR performance review.
The small builder fixture PE exceeds 10% byte growth because required canonical member-profile metadata crosses a 512-byte PE alignment boundary; this is not a measured Studio bundle-size change.
